title: fix: give negative ordinals the right suffix
description:
`ordinal()` picked the suffix from `n % 10`, which is `9` for `-1` in Python, so:

    >>> label_ordinal()([-1, -2, -3, -21])
    ['-1th', '-2th', '-3th', '-21th']

It now picks the suffix from the absolute value, giving `['-1st', '-2nd', '-3rd', '-21st']` (scales gives `-1st` too). `-11th`, `-12th` and `-13th` stay `th`.

Added cases to `test_label_ordinal` (they fail without the change) and a line to the changelog. The full test suite and `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` pass locally.

I used Claude Code to help find this and write the change.

Assisted-by: Claude Code

title: Build the documentation with great-docs and publish it on GitHub Pages
description:
Replace the Sphinx site on Read the Docs with a great-docs site on GitHub Pages.

## Changes

- Build the site with the new Documentation workflow on every push and pull request, and upload it so that `great-docs preview` can open it locally.
- Publish the site to GitHub Pages after a final release reaches PyPI, or on a manual run.
- Write docstrings in Markdown, with interlinks, dollar-sign maths, and Quarto code cells for examples.
- Run every example in the documentation build, which fails if one raises. Pytest no longer collects doctests; new tests cover the behaviours that only the doctests checked, and line coverage stays at 98.5%.
- Move each module's introductory prose to its section of the API reference.
- Add a script that checks the reference lists every name in each module's `__all__`. Great-docs does not read `__all__`.
- Add a landing page that explains what a scale computes and works through a linear and a log colour scale.
- Point the README link and badges to the new site and the test workflow.
- Credit Posit Software, PBC as the funder, and add colour to the navbar and content area.
- Correct docstring mistakes in `cubehelix_pal`, `breaks_width`, and a `label_number` example.

## Before merging

Switch the GitHub Pages source in the repository settings from the `main` branch to GitHub Actions. The deploy job uses `actions/deploy-pages`, which the branch source does not accept.

title: Fix missing values in discrete string palettes
description:
## Problem

`scale_discrete.map` converts palette output to a NumPy array. With a string palette, NumPy chooses a fixed-width string dtype. Assigning `na_value` silently truncates longer strings and stringifies `None` or `np.nan`.

For example, `scale_discrete.map(["a", None], lambda n: ["red"], ["a"], na_value="transparent")` currently returns `["red", "tra"]`; the default missing value becomes `"Non"` instead of `None`.

## Change

Convert a fixed-width string palette to object dtype only when missing inputs are present, before assigning the missing value. Numeric palettes and string palettes without missing inputs retain the existing path.

Regression tests cover list, Unicode-array, and byte-string-array palettes with `None`, `"transparent"`, and `np.nan`.

## Verification

• All 9 new regression cases failed on unchanged main (`f616dade`) and pass with the fix.
• Full suite including slow tests: 245 passed, 2 skipped (Python version guards).
• Ruff lint and format checks passed.
• Tested with Python 3.11 and NumPy 1.26.4.

title: fix: use the smallest gap between values in precision
description:
`precision()` takes the gap between the two smallest values, not the smallest gap, so uneven breaks get rounded too coarsely:

```python
>>> label_number()([0, 10, 10.5])
['0', '10', '10']       # now ['0.0', '10.0', '10.5']
>>> label_percent()([0, 0.10, 0.105])
['0%', '10%', '10%']    # now ['0.0%', '10.0%', '10.5%']
```

Repeated values had the same effect, since a zero first gap made it return 1. The fix drops repeats with `np.unique` and takes the smallest gap. The existing `precision` cases keep their results.

Added cases to `test_precision` (they fail without the fix) and a changelog entry. `pytest --runslow`, `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `pyright` all pass.

Found with [Bite](https://github.com/connabyss/bite), an AI bug finder.

title: ci: pin GitHub Actions to commit SHAs and update them
description:
Pin each third-party action to the commit of its latest release, with the version as a trailing comment. A moved tag can no longer change what runs in CI.

| Action | Old ref | New ref |
|---|---|---|
| `actions/checkout` | `v6` | `3d3c42e` (v7.0.1) |
| `astral-sh/setup-uv` | `v7` | `68559e9` (v10.3.3) |
| `codecov/codecov-action` | `v5` | `303a32d` (v7.1.1) |

`pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` stays on `release/v1`. Its README recommends that branch so that trusted-publishing fixes arrive automatically.

## Breaking changes

None of the breaking changes in the skipped major versions affect the inputs or triggers these workflows use.

- checkout v7 refuses to check out fork PRs under `pull_request_target` and `workflow_run`. These workflows use neither trigger.
- setup-uv v8 stopped publishing major and minor tags, which the SHA pin avoids.
- setup-uv v9 changed the `prune-cache` default to `false`, so the Actions cache may grow.
- setup-uv v10 turns off the default cache for `pull_request_target`, `workflow_run` and `release` events. `release.yml` runs on tag pushes, so caching still applies.
- codecov v6 and v7 move to Node 24 and change the signing-key account. The `fail_ci_if_error` and `name` inputs are unchanged.

title: Make pandas an optional dependency
description:
mizani imports pandas at the top of several modules, so every package that depends on mizani also depends on pandas. This PR removes those imports. mizani then works with numpy arrays and Python values without pandas installed, and behaves as before for pandas input.

The motivation is plotnine with polars dataframes and without pandas (has2k1/plotnine#602). I'll open that PR separately. It does not depend on this one, but plotnine can only drop pandas once a mizani release no longer requires it.

## How

- A new private module, `mizani/_pandas.py`, holds the pandas-aware checks: `is_series`, `is_categorical_dtype`, `is_timedelta` and `isna`. They use `get_pandas()`, which returns pandas from `sys.modules` only if it has already been imported. A pandas object can only exist if pandas has been imported, so the checks need no import, and mizani never imports pandas itself.
- The `isinstance(x, pd.Series)` and `pandas.api.types` checks use these helpers.
- The `pd.Timestamp` and `pd.Timedelta` checks are now `datetime.datetime` and `datetime.timedelta` checks. The pandas types subclass them, so pandas values still pass.
- `isna` is `pd.isna` when pandas is in use. Otherwise it is a numpy version that detects `None`, `NaN` and `NaT`.
- pandas is imported only under `TYPE_CHECKING`, for the type hints.
- python-dateutil is now an explicit dependency. mizani uses it, and it used to come in through pandas.
- pandas is in the `test` extra, because the tests use it.

## Testing

- The test suite passes: 185 passed, 1 skipped. I ran it in a fresh environment with `uv pip install -e ".[test]"`, as in CI.
- A new test, `tests/test_pandas_optional.py`, runs a subprocess in which pandas cannot be imported. It exercises bounds, breaks (including date and timedelta breaks), labels, palettes, scales and transforms, and checks that pandas was not imported.
- I also installed mizani without pandas and imported it.
- plotnine's test suite passes with this branch of mizani.

title: Apply accuracy rounding to number labels without scale_cut
description:
## Summary

Without `scale_cut`, `label_number(accuracy=5)([13])` returns `["13"]` even though the formatter computes the rounded value. Use that rounded value for ordinary number labels as well, preserving existing zero-scale behavior.

Add regression coverage for positive and negative values, rounding to zero, fractional accuracy, percentages, and neutral scale cuts, plus a changelog entry.

## Validation

- New regressions on original main: 4 failed, 3 passed; all 7 pass with the fix.
- Label tests and doctests: 56 passed.
- `python -m pytest -o addopts= tests -q --tb=short`: 189 passed, 3 skipped.
- Ruff lint/format checks for changed Python files and `git diff --check`: passed.

Prepared with OpenAI Codex; the diff was reviewed and these checks were run locally.

title: Allow negative integer powers in log and exp transforms
description:
`log_trans.inverse` and `exp_trans.transform` call `np.power(self.base, x)`. For `log10_trans` and `log2_trans` the base is the integer 10 or 2, so an integer array with a negative value raises:

```python
>>> log10_trans().inverse(np.array([-1, 0, 1]))
ValueError: Integers to negative integer powers are not allowed.
>>> exp_trans(2).transform(np.array([-1, 0, 1]))
ValueError: Integers to negative integer powers are not allowed.
```

This is the same numpy rule that #11 fixed for the log breaks. Casting the base to float makes numpy compute in floating point, so both now return `[0.1, 1, 10]` / `[0.5, 1, 2]`. Float inputs give the same results as before.

Added integer cases to `test_log10_trans` and `test_exp_trans` (they fail before the change). `pytest --runslow`, `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass locally. I left the changelog out to avoid a conflict with #86; happy to add a line once that one is settled.

title: Ignore missing values when rescale computes the input range
description:
`rescale`, `rescale_mid` and `rescale_max` take the input range from `np.min(x)` / `np.max(x)` when `_from` is not given. If `x` has a single `NaN`, the range becomes `(nan, nan)` and every output value is lost:

```python
>>> x = [1, 2, np.nan, 5]
>>> rescale(x)
array([nan, nan, nan, nan])
>>> rescale_mid(x, mid=1)
array([0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5])
>>> rescale_max(x)
array([nan, nan, nan, nan])
```

The R `scales` versions use `range(x, na.rm = TRUE)`, so only the missing value stays missing. This switches the three functions to `np.nanmin` / `np.nanmax`; results without missing values are unchanged.

With the change: `rescale(x)` gives `[0, 0.25, nan, 1]`, `rescale_mid(x, mid=1)` gives `[0.5, 0.625, nan, 1]` and `rescale_max(x)` gives `[0.2, 0.4, nan, 1]`.

Added cases to the three tests in `tests/test_bounds.py` (they fail before the change) and a changelog entry. `pytest --runslow`, `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass locally.

title: Keep the mantissa in mathtex labels of label_log
description:
With `mathtex=True`, `label_log` turns every exponential label into `$10^{exp}$` and drops the mantissa. `breaks_log` returns `1, 3, 10, 30, ...` style breaks for narrow ranges, so its own breaks get duplicated, wrong labels:

```python
>>> b = breaks_log()((1e-5, 5e-4))
>>> b
array([1.e-05, 3.e-05, 1.e-04, 3.e-04, 1.e-03])
>>> label_log(mathtex=True)(b)
['$10^{-5}$', '$10^{-5}$', '$10^{-4}$', '$10^{-4}$', '$10^{-3}$']
```

Without `mathtex` the same breaks are labelled `1e-5, 3e-5, ...`, so only the mathtex path loses information. Labels whose mantissa is not 1 are now written as `$3 \times 10^{-5}$`; powers of the base keep the current `$10^{-5}$` form.

Added a case to `test_label_log` (fails before the change). `pytest tests/test_labels.py`, `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass locally. I left the changelog out to avoid a conflict with #86; happy to add a line once that one is settled.

title: Add magnitude-based scaling to number labels
description:
This PR adds `scale_cut` support to `label_number`, allowing labels to rescale values and append suffixes according to their magnitude.

closes #71

title: Add for compact datetime labels
description: This PR adds `label_date_short` for compact labels on ordered datetime breaks. Each label shows changed calendar components and the smaller components needed for context.

title: Fall back to pandas to recognise null types
description: closes plotnine#1021

title: Fix named Brewer palettes selecting the wrong type
description:
This PR makes named Brewer palettes select their own type, so calls such as brewer_pal(palette="Set2") work without a matching type argument.

It also adds clear errors for unknown palette names, corrects the out-of-range palette message, and adds regression tests and changelog documentation.


resolves has2k1/plotnine#1048

title: Add placement parameter to extended_breaks
description:
This PRs adds a `placement` parameter to `breaks_extended` which controls the extreme ends of breaks to keep them `inside`, `flexible` or `loose`, or apply one mode to both ends.

closes #80.

title: BUG: Stop breaks_extended hanging when a pruning weight is 0
description:
Fixes #79

`breaks_extended` never returns if any of the first three pruning weights is 0: the search bound never drops. I now raise `ValueError` for non-positive weights, and the inner loop also bails if `step` overflows.

Tested with:
`pytest tests/test_breaks.py -k breaks_extended`

title: ENH: Accept a per-end only_inside in breaks_extended
description:
`only_inside` now also takes a pair `(lower, upper)`, one flag per end, so a break sequence can be held inside the limits at one end and allowed past them at the other. A single bool keeps its meaning for both ends, so nothing changes for existing callers.

The search itself is untouched. Talbot's coverage score is already a sum of one term per end, so the ends are scored independently; the flag only decides which candidates the search admits, and the per-end flag splits that check the same way. One example of the effect, at `n=3` on limits `(-7.7, 196.9)`: `only_inside=True` gives `[0, 90, 180]`, and `only_inside=(True, False)` gives `[0, 100, 200]`, because a labeling that ends past the data may now compete.

Motivation: a range frame that ends at a round number on one side and at the data on the other, for which the inside-only search picks a step that fits inside and then has to be padded, while the free-on-one-side search picks the step for the labeling that is actually drawn.

Adds a test for the pair, including the equivalence of `(flag, flag)` with `flag`, and a changelog entry under an unreleased v0.14.6 heading, which you may want to rename.

title: Fix numpy.timedelta DeprecationWarning on import
description:
From `numpy>=2.5.0` [release](https://github.com/numpy/numpy/releases/tag/v2.5.0)  there is a `DeprecationWarning` on the generic `np.datetime64("NaT")` initialisation, which gets called when importing `mizani._datetime.utils`

```
import warnings

warnings.simplefilter("error", DeprecationWarning)

# DeprecationWarning: The 'generic' unit for NumPy timedelta is deprecated
import mizani._datetime.utils
```
yields:
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "mizani/repro_script.py", line 6, in <module>
    import mizani._datetime.utils
  File "mizani/mizani/_datetime/utils.py", line 32, in <module>
    NaT_int = np.datetime64("NaT").astype(np.int64)
              ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
DeprecationWarning: The 'generic' unit for NumPy timedelta is deprecated, and will raise an error in the future. This includes implicit conversion of bare integers (e.g. `+ 1`).Please use a specific unit instead.
```

This PR resolves this DeprecationWarning by explicitly checking `np.isnat(x)` rather than comparing equality to `np.datetime64("NaT")`

title: Nominal scales are name only
description:
I did not read the reference, but the scale that applies to items only being 
related among each other per equality relation is called nominal and not norminal.

This is a nit only, but as documentation targets the readers understanding it may be worth the change.

Nominal comes from the Latin nomen which means name, we can at least identify and thus name the
Items. No norm is possible, and no ordering is defined either - one has to apply a convention.

Resolves #23 

PS: I provide this PR with good intentions not knowing if the changes align with the goals of the contributors, so no hard feelings if you choose to not include them. Thanks a lot for sharing the code.

title: Switch to use of np.power instead of ** for exps
description: I was trying to use a "custom" transform in plotnine, ```Python from mizani.transforms import exp_trans exp10 = exp_trans(10) qplot("carat", "price", data = diamondsk, log="xy") + \ coord_trans(x=exp10, y = exp10) ``` But this didn't work because it gives the error: because plotnine is passing in a tuple of limits but base `**` operator will not "broadcast" correctly and apply the exp on each element in the tuple. I think this should fix this. I also changed the inverse of log transform to match (I'm guessing that's why the try-catch was necessary there).

title: Fix guarding scipy import.
description:
Since probability_trans is called from the top-level of the module,
9885293 still left scipy required. With this it's no longer required.

title: Fix log_breaks for base 2 for values less than 1
description: fixes #17

title: Use chain.from_iterable in utils.py
description: This is a faster and more idiomatic way of using `itertools.chain`. Instead of computing all the items in the iterable and storing them in memory, they are computed one-by-one and never stored as a huge list. This can save on both runtime and memory space.

title: prevent integer overflow in log breaks
description: fixes has2k1/plotnine#320

title: Fixed raising integer to negative numpy integers
description:
Previously this error was sometimes raised in `breaks`
if a base was being raised to a numpy array that
included negative integers:
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/43287311/why-cant-i-raise-to-a-negative-power-in-numpy

Fixed this by making the dtype of the array that is
the exponent a float.

title: add squish
description:
behavior is similar to [scales](https://github.com/hadley/scales/blob/master/R/bounds.r#L175) but without a `finite_only` parameter.

follow up to https://github.com/has2k1/plotnine/issues/126

title: Explicitly cast log_breaks as float
description:
There seem to recently have been a change to Numpy to be more strict about e.g

`10 ** np.arange(-4, 4)`

This code above produces a `ValueError` in Numpy 1.13.0. Explicitly setting the `dtype` of `np.arange` solves the issue.

This prevents `ValueError: Integers to negative integer powers are not allowed.`
